label.en: Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion

translationRepairs: Wang Shan, whose style was Zaosru, came from Taicang in Jiangnan. He was the grandson of the Ming Grand Secretary Xijue.
Wang Shan, whose style was Zaoru, came from Taicang in Jiangnan. He was the grandson of the Ming Grand Secretary Xijue.
s0004 gives 字藻儒; 藻儒 is Zaoru, so idiomatic Zaosru is a misspelling. The proposed Zaoru restores the correct courtesy name without other changes.
Wang Shan, style Zaosru, was a native of Taicang in Jiangnan; he was the grandson of Xijue, Grand Secretary of the Ming.
Wang Shan, style Zaoru, was a native of Taicang in Jiangnan; he was the grandson of Xijue, Grand Secretary of the Ming.
The same 藻儒 requires Zaoru in the literal field; Zaosru is a misspelling, and the proposed replacement is accurate.
In 1691 he was specially promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
In 1691 he was specially promoted to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
s0011 has 超擢內閣學士; 內閣學士 is Academician of the Grand Secretariat, distinct from 大學士 Grand Secretary. The prior idiomatic conflates the ranks; the proposed title is correct.
In the thirtieth year he was promoted by special selection to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
In the thirtieth year he was promoted by special selection to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
Literal likewise renders 內閣學士 as Grand Secretary; Academician of the Grand Secretariat matches the Chinese office and leaves the rest of the sentence intact.
